## R Markdown

```{R}
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Define your months/folders
months <- c("October", "November", "December")

# 2. Identify the 7 unique file names (assuming they are the same in all folders)
# We'll use December as the template
file_names <- list.files(path = "December", pattern = "\\.parquet$")

# 3. Create the 7 combined dataframes
# We loop through each file name, read it from every folder, and bind them
combined_data <- map(file_names, function(file) {
  
  # Construct paths for this specific file across all months
  paths <- file.path(months, file)
  
  # Read and stack them
  # map_df automatically rbinds the results into one dataframe
  map_df(paths, read_parquet)
})

# 4. Name the list elements so you can access them easily
# e.g., combined_data$players.parquet
names(combined_data) <- file_names

# 5. (Optional) Bring them into the global environment as individual objects
# This creates 7 dataframes in your environment named after the files
list2env(combined_data, .GlobalEnv)

# Verify the results
cat("Combined dataframes created:", paste(names(combined_data), collapse = ", "))

```

```{R}

library(tidyverse)


# 2. Extract Play-Level Base Data (Lineups and Scores)
# We take distinct play_ids to ensure one row per play
play_base <- stats_and_plays %>%
  select(
    play_id = `plays.id`,
    away_score,
    home_score,
    # Lineup IDs
    off1.id, off2.id, off3.id, off4.id, off5.id,
    def1.id, def2.id, def3.id, def4.id, def5.id
  ) %>%
  distinct(play_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3. Extract Shot Clock Information
# Filtering for the 'short_clock' identifier in the conditions table
shot_clock_info <- conditions %>%
  filter(id == "short_clock") %>%
  select(play_id = `plays.id`, shot_clock_status = description) %>%
  distinct(play_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 4. Extract Expected Points (xPts)
# Filtering for the 'xpt' stat in the advanced_stats table
expected_pts_info <- advanced_stats %>%
  filter(stat == "xpt") %>%
  select(play_id = `plays.id`, expectedPts = value) %>%
  distinct(play_id, .keep_all = TRUE)


pramit_dataset <- play_base %>%
  left_join(shot_clock_info, by = "play_id") %>%
  left_join(expected_pts_info, by = "play_id") %>%
  # Organize columns for the final model
  select(
    play_id,
    away_score,
    home_score,
    shot_clock_status,
    expectedPts,
    starts_with("off"),
    starts_with("def")
  )

# Preview the result
print(head(pramit_dataset))

pramit_dataset %>% write.csv("gen_info_plays.csv")
# Export the final dataset
# write_csv(pramit_dataset, "pramit_overall_statistics.csv")
```

## Mixed Effects Model

```{R}
library(lme4)
all_screens$screener_id <- as.factor(all_screens$screener_id)
all_screens$screen_bh   <- as.factor(all_screens$screen_bh)
all_screens$screen_bhd  <- as.factor(all_screens$screen_bhd)
all_screens$screen_scrd <- as.factor(all_screens$screen_scrd)
all_screens$shot_type <- as.factor(all_screens$shot_type)
all_screens$shot_contest_type <- as.factor(all_screens$shot_contest_type)
all_screens$screen_defense <- as.factor(all_screens$screen_defense)
all_screens$make = as.factor(all_screens$make)
screen_model <- glmer(make ~ shot_distance + screen_type + screen_defense + shot_contest_type +
              (1 | screener_id) + 
              (1 | screen_bh) + 
              (1 | screen_bhd) + 
              (1 | screen_scrd), 
              data = all_screens, 
              family = binomial(link = "logit"),
              nAGQ = 0, 
              control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

screen_model %>% summary()
```

##New Approach rankings

```{R}
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
advanced_stats = combined_data[[2]]
ids_to_name = advanced_stats %>% distinct(name, id)
all_effects <- ranef(screen_model)
# 1. Prepare player-specific shot values
# Create a helper function to get the average shot value for each role
get_player_avg_value <- function(role_name) {
  col_name <- role_name
  
  all_screens %>%
    group_by(player_id = as.character(.data[[col_name]])) %>%
    summarise(avg_shot_value = mean(ifelse(fg_type == "fg3", 3, 2), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
}

# 2. Update ranking function to use specific weights
get_epa_rankings <- function(role_name, sort_desc = TRUE) {
  # Get global intercept
  global_intercept <- fixef(screen_model)["(Intercept)"]
  
  # Get player specific average shot values
  player_values <- get_player_avg_value(role_name)
  
  # Build base dataframe - ensure player_id is character to match the join
  df_role <- data.frame(
    player_id = as.character(rownames(all_effects[[role_name]])),
    random_effect = all_effects[[role_name]][["(Intercept)"]],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Merge with values
  # Explicitly convert player_values$player_id to character just in case
  df_role <- df_role %>%
    mutate(player_id = as.character(player_id)) %>%
    left_join(player_values %>% mutate(player_id = as.character(player_id)), by = "player_id") %>%
    mutate(
      baseline_prob = plogis(global_intercept),
      player_prob = plogis(global_intercept + random_effect),
      prob_lift = player_prob - baseline_prob,
      expected_points_added = prob_lift * avg_shot_value
    )
  
  if(sort_desc) {
    return(df_role[order(-df_role$expected_points_added), ])
  } else {
    return(df_role[order(df_role$expected_points_added), ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate rankings
rankings_screener <- get_epa_rankings("screener_id", sort_desc = TRUE)
rankings_bh <- get_epa_rankings("screen_bh", sort_desc = TRUE)
rankings_bhd <- get_epa_rankings("screen_bhd", sort_desc = FALSE) # Lower is better for defenders
rankings_scrd <- get_epa_rankings("screen_scrd", sort_desc = FALSE)

# 4. Join with names
ids_to_name = ids_to_name %>% mutate(id = as.factor(id))
rankings_screener <- rankings_screener %>% left_join(ids_to_name, by = c("player_id" = "id"))
rankings_bh <- rankings_bh %>% left_join(ids_to_name, by = c("player_id" = "id"))
rankings_bhd <- rankings_bhd %>% left_join(ids_to_name, by = c("player_id" = "id"))
rankings_scrd <- rankings_scrd %>% left_join(ids_to_name, by = c("player_id" = "id"))

rankings_bh %>% colnames()
```

```{R}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggExtra)
combined_epa <- rankings_bh %>%
  select(player_id, name, epa_bh = expected_points_added) %>%
  inner_join(rankings_screener %>% select(player_id, epa_screener = expected_points_added), by = "player_id")

# 2. Identify the IDs to label
# Get Top 5 / Bottom 5 for BH
top_bh <- combined_epa %>% slice_max(epa_bh, n = 5) %>% pull(player_id)
bot_bh <- combined_epa %>% slice_min(epa_bh, n = 5) %>% pull(player_id)

# Get Top 5 / Bottom 5 for Screener
top_scr <- combined_epa %>% slice_max(epa_screener, n = 5) %>% pull(player_id)
bot_scr <- combined_epa %>% slice_min(epa_screener, n = 5) %>% pull(player_id)

# Specific players to highlight
highlight_names <- c("Draymond Green", "Stephen Curry", "LeBron James", "Jaylen Brown", "Jalen Duren")

# 3. Create a label column
combined_epa <- combined_epa %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(
    player_id %in% c(top_bh, bot_bh, top_scr, bot_scr) ~ name,
    name %in% highlight_names ~ name,
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# 4. Generate the plot
p <- ggplot(combined_epa, aes(x = epa_screener, y = epa_bh)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Expected Points Added: Ball Handler vs. Screener",
    x = "Screener EPA",
    y = "Ball Handler EPA"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# 5. Add marginal histograms
ggExtra::ggMarginal(p, type = "histogram", bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white")
```

```{R}

get_epa_rankings_with_ci <- function(role_name) {
  # 1. Setup
  global_intercept <- fixef(screen_model)["(Intercept)"]
  player_values <- get_player_avg_value(role_name)
  
  # Extract BLUPs and conditional variances
  # postVar is [1, 1, N], so we take [1, 1, ]
  random_effects <- all_effects[[role_name]][["(Intercept)"]]
  conditional_vars <- attr(all_effects[[role_name]], "postVar")[1, 1, ]
  
  # 2. Build data frame
  df_role <- data.frame(
    player_id = as.character(rownames(all_effects[[role_name]])),
    random_effect = random_effects,
    se_eta = sqrt(conditional_vars),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # 3. Join with values and calculate EPA and SE
  df_role <- df_role %>%
    left_join(player_values %>% mutate(player_id = as.character(player_id)), by = "player_id") %>%
    mutate(
      baseline_prob = plogis(global_intercept),
      player_prob = plogis(global_intercept + random_effect),
      prob_lift = player_prob - baseline_prob,
      expected_points_added = prob_lift * avg_shot_value,
      # Delta method: SE = avg_value * p * (1-p) * SE_eta
      se_epa = avg_shot_value * (player_prob * (1 - player_prob)) * se_eta,
      lower_ci = expected_points_added - (1.96 * se_epa),
      upper_ci = expected_points_added + (1.96 * se_epa)
    )
  
  # 4. Filter top 5 and bottom 5
  top_5 <- df_role %>% arrange(desc(expected_points_added)) %>% head(5) %>% mutate(rank_group = "Top 5")
  bottom_5 <- df_role %>% arrange(expected_points_added) %>% head(5) %>% mutate(rank_group = "Bottom 5")
  
  return(bind_rows(top_5, bottom_5))
}

# Generate final reports for each role
roles <- c("screener_id", "screen_bh", "screen_bhd", "screen_scrd")
final_rankings <- lapply(roles, get_epa_rankings_with_ci)
names(final_rankings) <- roles

# Join with names for final output
# Assuming ids_to_name is already a data frame with 'id' and 'name'
final_rankings <- lapply(final_rankings, function(df) {
  df %>% 
    mutate(player_id = as.factor(player_id)) %>%
    left_join(ids_to_name %>% mutate(id = as.factor(id)), by = c("player_id" = "id"))
})
```



```{R}
library(performance)

# Calculate ICC for all random effects
icc_results <- icc(screen_model)

# Print results
print(icc_results)

# Extract variance components
var_comp <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(screen_model))

# Residual variance for logit link is pi^2 / 3
residual_var <- (pi^2) / 3

# Filter to get only the random effects variance
random_effect_vars <- var_comp %>%
  filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
  select(grp, vcov)

# Calculate total variance (sum of random effect variances + residual variance)
total_variance <- sum(random_effect_vars$vcov) + residual_var

# Calculate ICC for each group
icc_distribution <- random_effect_vars %>%
  mutate(icc = vcov / total_variance) %>%
  select(grp, icc)

# Display the distribution of variance
print(icc_distribution)

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(icc_distribution, aes(x = grp, y = icc)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Variance Partitioning (ICC) by Role",
       x = "Random Effect Group",
       y = "Proportion of Variance Explained")
```

```{R}

defensive_indices <- c(3, 4)
defensive_roles <- c("BH Defender", "Screen Defender")

# Plotting function for defenders
plot_defensive_rankings <- function(df, role_label) {
  
  # Sorting: Reorder names by -EPA to put lowest (best) EPA at the top
  df$name <- reorder(df$name, -df$expected_points_added)
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = expected_points_added, y = name, color = rank_group)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci), height = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    # Ensure Top 5 (Best/Low EPA) and Bottom 5 (Worst/High EPA) are visually distinct
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Top 5" = "#0072B2", "Bottom 5" = "#D55E00")) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Defensive EPA Rankings:", role_label),
      subtitle = "Top 5 (Lowest EPA) vs Bottom 5 (Highest EPA)",
      x = "Expected Points Added (EPA)",
      y = "Player Name",
      color = "Performance Rank"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}

# Generate plots
for (i in seq_along(defensive_indices)) {
  df_idx <- defensive_indices[i]
  role_name <- defensive_roles[i]
  
  p <- plot_defensive_rankings(final_rankings[[df_idx]], role_name)
  print(p)
}
```


```{R}

fixed_effects_summary <- summary(screen_model)$coefficients

# Filter for the screen_type variables
# Assumes your model output contains variables like "screen_typehedge", 
# "screen_typeswitch", etc.
screen_type_effects <- data.frame(
  screen_type = rownames(fixed_effects_summary),
  estimate = fixed_effects_summary[, "Estimate"]
) %>%
  filter(grepl("screen_type", screen_type))

# Re-calculate the absolute impact for each type
# The intercept represents the reference level
intercept <- fixed_effects_summary["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]

screen_type_effects <- screen_type_effects %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean the name to remove "screen_type"
    screen_type = gsub("screen_type", "", screen_type),
    # Calculate the total effect
    # Note: If the reference level is not in the coefficients table, 
    # you may need to add a row manually for the intercept value itself.
    total_impact = intercept + estimate
  ) %>%
  arrange(-total_impact)
```

```{R}

fixed_effects_summary <- summary(screen_model)$coefficients

# Filter for the screen_defense variables
# 'screen_defense' will be expanded into multiple rows (one for each type)
# The first level (e.g., "drop") is usually the intercept, 
# and the others are deviations from it.
screen_type_effects <- data.frame(
  screen_type = rownames(fixed_effects_summary),
  estimate = fixed_effects_summary[, "Estimate"]
) %>%
  filter(grepl("screen_defense", screen_type))

# Re-calculate the absolute impact for each type
# The intercept represents the reference level (the first alphabetical level)
# We add the intercept to the deviations to get the true effect
intercept <- fixed_effects_summary["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]
screen_type_effects <- screen_type_effects %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean the name to remove "screen_defense"
    screen_type = gsub("screen_defense", "", screen_type),
    # Calculate the total effect
    total_impact = intercept + estimate
  ) %>%
  arrange(-total_impact)
```

```{R}
# Filter for the screen_type variables

# The intercept represents the reference level
intercept <- fixed_effects_summary["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]

screen_type_effects <- screen_type_effects %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean the name to remove "screen_type"
    screen_type = gsub("screen_type", "", screen_type),
    # Calculate the total effect
    # Note: If the reference level is not in the coefficients table, 
    # you may need to add a row manually for the intercept value itself.
    total_impact = intercept + estimate
  ) %>%
  arrange(-total_impact)
```


```{R}

library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggExtra)

# Prepare the data
comparison_df <- rankings_bh %>%
  rename(bh_impact = impact_coefficient) %>%
  left_join(rankings_screener %>% select(player_id, impact_coefficient), by = "player_id") %>%
  rename(screener_impact = impact_coefficient)

# Define specific players to label
players_to_label <- c("Stephen Curry", "Nikola Jokic", "Draymond Green", "LeBron James")

# Create the scatterplot
p <- ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = bh_impact, y = screener_impact)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "midnightblue") +
  geom_text_repel(data = subset(comparison_df, name %in% players_to_label),
                  aes(label = name), box.padding = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Player Impact: Ball Handling vs. Screening",
       x = "Ball Handler Impact (Random Effect)",
       y = "Screener Impact (Random Effect)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Add histograms to the axes
ggMarginal(p, type = "histogram", fill = "steelblue", color = "white")
```

```{R}
var_comp <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(screen_model))

# 2. Filter out Residual and calculate Relative ICC
relative_icc_data <- var_comp %>%
  filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
  mutate(grp = recode(grp, "screen_bh" = "Ball Handler", 
                           "screener_id" = "Screener", 
                           "screen_scrd" = "Screener Def", 
                           "screen_bhd" = "BH Def")) %>%
  mutate(relative_percent = (vcov / sum(vcov)) * 100)

# 3. Plot
ggplot(relative_icc_data, aes(x = reorder(grp, relative_percent), y = relative_percent, fill = grp)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Relative Variance Partitioning",
       subtitle = "Proportion of player-attributable variation by role",
       x = "Player Role", y = "Relative ICC (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
```

```{R}
top_10 <- rankings_screener %>%
  slice_max(impact_coefficient, n = 10)

bottom_10 <- rankings_screener %>%
  slice_min(impact_coefficient, n = 10)

plot_data <- bind_rows(top_10, bottom_10) %>%
  # Arrange so the plot displays from highest to lowest
  arrange(impact_coefficient) %>%
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = name))

# 2. Create the Plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = name, y = impact_coefficient, fill = impact_coefficient > 0)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() + # Makes it a horizontal bar chart
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2ecc71", "FALSE" = "#e74c3c"), 
                    guide = "none") +
  # Add the labels on the bars
  geom_text(aes(label = round(impact_coefficient, 4)), 
            hjust = ifelse(plot_data$impact_coefficient > 0, -0.1, 1.1),
            size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 and Bottom 10 Screeners by Impact Coefficient",
       subtitle = "Random effect estimates controlling for situation",
       x = "Player Name",
       y = "Impact Coefficient (Deviation from Average)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  # Expand y-axis limits to make room for labels
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.2, 0.2)))
```
